title: MemoryEvaluation
description: Groq-powered memory importance evaluation schema. Used with response_format.json_schema.strict=true to guarantee structured output from reasoning models.

importance_score.description: Importance score from 0.0 (trivial) to 1.0 (critical). Determines pruning action: <0.3 archive, 0.3-0.7 condense, >=0.7 keep.

should_keep.description: Whether this memory should be kept in active storage. True for importance >= 0.3.

condensed_version.description: Shorter version of the memory content if condensing (0.3-0.7 range). Null if keeping unchanged or archiving.

reasoning.description: Brief explanation of why this score was assigned. Should reference specific content that informed the decision.

tags.description: Category tags for this memory. Common tags: identity, failure, preference, architecture, decision, debug, status, temporary.

x-score-criteria.description: Scoring guidelines for evaluators. These criteria ensure consistent evaluation across models and runs.

tiers.label: Critical — Core Identity
tiers.description: Core identity elements, catastrophic failure lessons, fundamental user preferences. Losing this would change who the agent is.
indicators: Agent name, principles, voice, north star
Hard-won lessons from system failures or data loss
User preferences confirmed across multiple interactions

tiers.label: High — Project Context & Decisions
tiers.description: Architectural decisions, project-specific knowledge, integration patterns. Valuable context that took effort to acquire.

tiers.label: Medium — Routine Logs
tiers.description: Task completion notes, status updates, routine operational logs. Contains some useful context but verbose.
indicators: Daily task logs with mixed relevance
Meeting notes with some action items

tiers.label: Low — Debug & Temporary
tiers.description: Debug output, temporary scratch notes, stale context from completed tasks. Safe to archive.
indicators: Raw debug output or stack traces
Temporary notes for a completed one-off task
Outdated environment details (old versions, removed deps)
Exploratory scratch work that led nowhere

x-examples.input_summary: SOUL.md — Agent identity: name 'Artemis', principles: 'never delete user data without confirmation', voice: 'concise, technical'

evaluation.reasoning: Core identity file defining agent name, principles, and communication style. Loss would fundamentally alter agent behavior and identity continuity.

x-examples.input_summary: Lesson learned: never run 'rm -rf' on workspace without checkpoint. Lost 3 days of work on 2026-01-15.

evaluation.reasoning: Hard-won failure lesson about destructive operations. This type of knowledge prevents future catastrophic mistakes and should be preserved permanently.

x-examples.input_summary: Architecture notes: OpenClaw gateway binds to loopback:18789 with token auth. Telegram bot uses getMe for validation. AMCP checkpoints use CIDv1 with SHA-256.

evaluation.reasoning: Architectural context about gateway configuration, bot integration, and checkpoint format. Took effort to learn and is actively referenced during operations.

x-examples.input_summary: 2026-02-10 work log: Fixed 3 flaky tests in solvr-pinning.bats by adding mock curl responses. Updated pin-to-solvr.sh to send progress to stderr. Ran full test suite — 115 pass, 3 pre-existing failures. Also reviewed PR #42 comments.

evaluation.condensed_version: Fixed flaky solvr-pinning tests (mock curl). pin-to-solvr.sh: progress to stderr. 115/118 tests pass.
evaluation.reasoning: Daily work log with useful but verbose details. The fixes and test results are worth keeping in condensed form; PR review details and step-by-step narrative can be dropped.

x-examples.input_summary: Troubleshooting session: tried 5 different approaches to fix AgentMail auth. Approach 1: used v1 API — failed 404. Approach 2: used v0 API — failed 401. Approach 3: added Bearer prefix — failed 401. Approach 4: checked inbox format — was wrong. Approach 5: used correct inbox@agentmail.to format — worked.

evaluation.condensed_version: AgentMail auth: use v0 API with inbox@agentmail.to format. v1 API returns 404. Bearer auth required.
evaluation.reasoning: Verbose troubleshooting with 5 attempts. The conclusion (v0 API + correct inbox format) is valuable; the step-by-step trial narrative is not. Condense to outcome.

x-examples.input_summary: Debug output from checkpoint.sh test run: [2026-02-08T14:23:01] Creating staging dir... [14:23:02] Copying identity.json... [14:23:02] Running scan_for_secrets... [14:23:03] 0 secrets found... [14:23:03] Calling amcp checkpoint create... [output continues for 200 lines]

evaluation.reasoning: Raw debug output from a routine test run. No failures or unusual behavior recorded. This is transient operational data with no long-term value.

x-examples.input_summary: Scratch notes: 'TODO check if jq 1.6 handles null differently than 1.7... also look at that weird curl timeout... maybe related to DNS? need coffee'

evaluation.reasoning: Stream-of-consciousness scratch notes with no actionable conclusions. The jq version question and curl timeout were never resolved or documented. Safe to archive.

json_schema.schema: Reference to the main schema above (properties, required, additionalProperties)

notes: strict: true ensures Groq returns ONLY the fields defined in the schema
additionalProperties: false prevents extra fields in the response
condensed_version uses type ['string', 'null'] for nullable support
temperature 0.1 for consistent scoring across evaluations
